scope: One private Python/SQLite profile API behind the existing HTTPS site; frontend remains a separate static build.
status: implemented-and-locally-tested; deployment owned by parent agent

authentication.username: 3–32 ASCII letters/digits/_/-, first alphanumeric; case-insensitive identity; preserved display capitalization
authentication.pin: Six digits; repeated-digit and consecutive ascending/descending sequences refused at registration
authentication.verifier: scrypt N=32768, r=8, p=3, 32-byte output and a random 16-byte salt per profile; HMAC-SHA256 with a separate private 32-byte pepper precedes scrypt.
authentication.secretHandling: The PIN is never returned, logged, placed in URLs or stored as plaintext. The pepper file has mode 0600 and is separate from the database; startup never generates or replaces it. The user chooses their real PIN in the app.
authentication.session: A random 256-bit opaque token; only its SHA-256 digest is stored. HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict and __Host cookie attributes; 30-day expiry; at most ten sessions per profile.
authentication.throttling: Durable SQLite limits: five attempts per account per 15 minutes, thirty per client IP per 15 minutes and ten registrations per IP per hour. X-Real-IP is accepted only from configured exact proxy addresses.
authentication.capacity: At most 100 profiles, a bounded rate table, sixteen simultaneous connections and two simultaneous scrypt operations.
authentication.recovery: No username-only reset or public account list. A forgotten PIN requires deliberate private operator recovery.

progress.atomicity: Optimistic integer revisions, an immediate SQLite transaction and a conditional UPDATE. A stale revision returns 409 and leaves the stored record unchanged.
progress.identityGuard: GET includes the signed-in username. PUT requires a matching username so a stale open tab cannot write to another profile after the shared cookie changes.
progress.validation: Version1 and required envelope types; bounded JSON depth/members; reject duplicate/reservedprototype keys and nonfinite numbers. Browser performs full activity/catalogue validation.
progress.restart: Sessions, throttles and progress persist in the private SQLite volume. The separate pepper must be retained.

http.mutations: Mutations require the exact same-origin Origin header and JSON content type. No CORS access; cross-site Fetch Metadata is rejected.
http.cache: All responses use no-store, nosniff and same-origin CORP.
http.logging: Request and error logs are suppressed in the service. The proxy location must also disable access logs.
http.development: An explicit development flag permits a separate insecure cookie only with a loopback bind and local HTTP origin.

scenarios: PIN, salt, session and pepper secrecy
Different salts and hashes for the same PIN across profiles
Generic wrong and unknown credential errors
Untrusted IP headers cannot bypass limits
Origin, content type and HTTP method guards
Common PIN and oversized or invalid progress rejection
Concurrent writes cannot both use the same stale revision

deploymentRequirements: Build from server/ only; never include private data or the repository root.
Resolve the Python base image tag to a digest before production.
Run as nonroot with a read-only root, bounded resources and dedicated private persistent state.
Mount the owner-only pepper separately, read-only, and retain it across releases.
Keep the backend port private and trust only the exact proxy address.
Preserve the API prefix and original Origin; overwrite X-Real-IP; cap bodies at 8002048 bytes; disable caching and access logs.
limitations: A short PIN has low entropy. The separate pepper and online attempt limits reduce risk, but compromise of the whole server can expose records and the key.
No external penetration test or security certification is claimed.
The server validates a bounded JSON envelope, not linguistic accuracy or genuine activity completion.
No real learner record or existing database was accessed; all test data is disposable.
